nodes.state:
The FDA May 2022 recall includes Jif 16 ounce creamy peanut butter, identifier
5150025516 as printed in the notice. A jar is in scope when the first seven
digits of its lot code are between 1274425 and 2140425 and end in 425. The
range alone is insufficient. This is the published scope for this historical
example.

questions.prompt: How should a jar be matched to this recall?

options.label: Match the product and both lot-code conditions
Use the product name alone
Request a clearer recall notice

nodes.state:
Illustrative warehouse inventory: 40 sealed jars have lot code 1352425, 10
have lot code 1352426, and 6 have unreadable lot codes. All are Jif 16 ounce
creamy peanut butter, identifier 5150025516. No other jars are on hand.

questions.prompt: Can every jar in this inventory be matched to an identifiable lot?

nodes.state:
Illustrative records at 09:30 on May 23, 2022: ingredient lot 1352425 was used
in 60 snack boxes, batch SNACK-A. Harbor received 30 and Summit received 30.
Harbor acknowledges the recall notice and confirms all 30 are isolated. Summit
has not responded. There were no other shipments of this batch.

questions.prompt: Which customer needs a response follow-up first?

options.label: Contact Harbor
Contact Summit
Contact both customers again

nodes.state:
Our example stock policy is to quarantine confirmed recalled jars and hold
unreadable codes for identification. Apply the scope only to products and lots
it actually covers.

questions.prompt: What should the warehouse do with its stock?

options.label: Quarantine matching jars and hold unreadable codes for identification
Hold every jar pending further review
Identify unreadable codes before choosing any stock action

nodes.state:
Apply the recall scope to ingredient lot 1352425 and the snack boxes made from
it. Following recall communication guidance, establish that affected customers
received and followed the notice. Under our example response policy, missing
acknowledgment requires direct follow-up; reported sales require escalation
and verification of downstream notification. Use the latest dated response for
each customer.

questions.prompt: What customer follow-up is needed now?

options.label: Ask Summit to acknowledge the notice and account for its boxes
Verify that both customers have isolated all affected boxes
Escalate reported sales to the recall lead and verify downstream notification

nodes.state:
Combine the warehouse and customer decisions into a recommendation for the
recall lead. A warehouse hold does not account for shipped products.
Coordinate any unresolved customer or downstream follow-up alongside the stock
action. Use the latest dated customer records.

questions.prompt: Which response should the recall lead coordinate?

options.label: Coordinate warehouse holds only
Coordinate warehouse holds and missing customer responses
Coordinate warehouse holds and escalation of sales to end customers
